blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A service on the course runner's OR-Tools 9.15.6755 wheel calls `mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.GLPK)` on a small LP. What happens?

options.text: It solves the LP, since GLPK is an open-source solver the wheel bundles
options.says: The lesson's survey shows GLPK refused: 'solver type SOLVER_TYPE_GLPK is not registered'.

options.text: It solves the LP with HiGHS, since MathOpt falls back to a solver that it does have
options.says: No fallback happened for any absent solver in the survey; each was refused with an exception.

options.text: It raises before solving, since GLPK has a SolverType name but no compiled code
options.says: Right: five SolverType members, GLPK among them, are not registered in this build, and solve raises.

options.text: It returns INFEASIBLE, since a solver that is absent finds no feasible point
options.says: An absent solver is a refusal, raised as an exception, never a termination status.

origin.section: Each API Has Its Own List of Backends, and Only Some Are Compiled In

questions.stem: Inherited code calls `pywraplp.Solver.CreateSolver("GLOP")`, makes the truck count an `IntVar`, and checks only that `Solve()` returned `OPTIMAL`. What can it get back?

options.text: A fractional truck count, since the wrapper's GLOP solves the LP relaxation
options.says: Right: the lesson's wrapper GLOP took an integer variable, said OPTIMAL and returned b = 3.5487.

options.text: An exception, since GLOP refuses any model that has an integer variable
options.says: That is MathOpt's GLOP; the wrapper's GLOP raised nothing and returned OPTIMAL.

options.text: The status ABNORMAL, since GLOP reports integer variables it cannot handle
options.says: ABNORMAL came from BOP given a continuous variable; GLOP returned OPTIMAL.

options.text: A whole truck count, since GLOP rounds every integer variable after solving
options.says: The lesson's run returned b = 3.5487, not a whole number.

origin.section: Each API Reports a Refusal in Its Own Place

questions.stem: A colleague says the course runner's MathOpt would solve with Gurobi if a license file were mounted. What do the lesson's runs show?

options.text: That is right, since the gurobipy wheel ships a library that MathOpt loads
options.says: Pointed at that library, MathOpt aborted with exit code -6 on a missing GRBcopyparams.

options.text: That is right, since the error MathOpt gave was about the missing license
options.says: The error was a bad_function_call, and the loader stopped before any license was looked for.

options.text: That is wrong, since SolverType in this build has no member at all for the Gurobi solver
options.says: SolverType.GUROBI exists; the survey lists it, and it fails when solving.

options.text: That is wrong, since loading the wheel's library aborts before any license check
options.says: Right: OR-Tools 9.15 needs GRBcopyparams, which the gurobipy 13 library lacks, so both APIs abort.

origin.section: Gurobi Is on Every List, and Loads Through Neither API in the Course Runner
